title: The window between accepted and committed
request:
A write at the head, read from the tail before and after it propagates

./your_program.sh chain
init 3
write k 7
read k
read-at 0 k
propagate
read k
note: Both answers are correct at the moment they are given. The head has the write and the tail does not, and the rule that reads come from the tail is what turns that into a consistent story rather than a race.

title: Losing the middle of the chain
request:
A committed write, a second in flight, and then the middle node dies

./your_program.sh chain
init 3
write k 7
propagate
write k 9
fail 1
propagate
read k
note: The second write had reached node 1 and no further. Node 1's predecessor still holds it, so closing the chain is enough to finish delivering it — no consensus round, no reconciliation, just the prefix invariant doing the work.
